Japan's agriculture minister, Kazuo Yana, didn't exactly get fired. He resigned on October 14, 2026, and Takaichi accepted, which Jiji Press described as an effective dismissal. Yana was mired in a series of scandals, including suspected election law violations, and his departure dealt a serious blow to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration.

**What led to it:** Takaichi had appointed Yana in a cabinet reshuffle the previous month, then publicly rebuked him in parliament over remarks about road funding. He had come under fire for comments about cutting road funding for municipalities that did not support him. Yana confirmed the authenticity of an audio clip in which he said one reason for budget cuts in two municipalities in his constituency was their support of a rival candidate in a February parliamentary election. He has since denied having the power to sway such budget decisions, and his comment quickly drew widespread criticism as an abuse of power.

**Why he stepped down:** Yana said he didn't want to hinder parliamentary deliberations any further, and that he wanted to avoid being unable to focus on agricultural and fishery policy. Takaichi said the government "needs to work on important issues," mentioning legislation on a proposed consumption tax rate cut for food.

**Takaichi's response:** She said responsibility for appointing him rests upon her. Yana's replacement was to be announced on Thursday, October 15.

**Political context:** Opposition parties in the upper house, where the ruling coalition lacks a majority, were preparing a censure motion against Yana, while some threatened to block debate on the sales tax legislation until he stepped down. On October 12, 2026, North Korea fired several ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area into the Sea of Japan, and Japan's government confirmed the launches.

**Japan's assessment:** Defense minister Takashi Koyari said at least two missiles were fired. One flew about 220 km and peaked near 20 km in altitude, and the other flew about 910 km and peaked near 70 km. The missiles landed outside Japan's exclusive economic zone. Officials said the weapons "may have flown on irregular trajectories", and Japan, the US, and South Korea were analyzing them in detail. Japan's government passed the flight information to aircraft and ships nearby, and no reports of damage or other consequences had been received at the time of reporting.

**South Korea's account:** South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detected the launches at about 9:20 a.m. local time and said one of the missiles flew more than 900 kilometers. South Korea's presidential office called the launches violations of UN Security Council resolutions, and Japan and South Korea both condemned them as a threat to regional stability.

**Context:** The launch was the 16th round of ballistic missile launches this year by North Korea, according to Korea Herald reporting. It came after North Korea's October 3 missile test from Wonsan, which Pyongyang described as training for troops operating its hypersonic strategic weapons system. It also followed a September 21 land mine explosion in the Demilitarised Zone that injured three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously. Seoul blamed North Korean troops for planting the mines, and Pyongyang denied responsibility. Some outlets reported that the launch may have been a response to South Korea's own hypersonic glide vehicle test days earlier. North Korea has not issued any public statement on Monday's launches.

Sources differ slightly on details. Some reports describe the launches as "several" missiles, while Japan's government specifically confirmed at least two.

content.text:
Here are three of the biggest stories in Japan from October 12 to 19, 2026. Which stories matter most is my judgment.

1. **Farm minister quits over a scandal:** Agriculture Minister Kazuo Yana resigned on October 14, which Jiji called an effective dismissal, after a recording suggested he cut road budgets for towns that had backed a rival candidate; he is the first minister in Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's cabinet to leave over a scandal. [nippon.com / Jiji Press](https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2026101400736/)

2. **Nikkei's third-largest one-day fall:** On October 15 the Nikkei 225 dropped about 3,318 points to roughly 64,425, the third-biggest single-day point drop in its history. [Qatar News Agency](https://qna.org.qa/en/News-Area/News/2026-10/15/japans-nikkei-index-plunges-over-3300-points-in-third-largest-drop-in-history) (the exact figures come from [Jiji's economy headlines](https://www.jiji.com/jc/archives?g=eco_archive_0))

3. **North Korean missiles:** On October 12 North Korea fired at least two ballistic missiles into the Sea of Japan, one of them about 910 km, and Japan said they may have flown on irregular paths before landing outside its exclusive economic zone. [nippon.com / Jiji Press](https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2026101200185/)

I couldn't find a reliable report on what caused the October 15 stock drop.

Other stories this week: a record 4.28 million foreign residents in Japan, a swine fever outbreak in Ibaraki, and fixes after a false earthquake early warning from the Japan Meteorological Agency.
